class.name: CVars
class.description: Singleton that stores named int, float, bool, and [String] values which can be changed while the project is running. Writes carry a priority. A lower priority source cannot replace a higher one. From lowest to highest: constructor, project setting, config file, command line, code, then the console. Setting the same value again still raises the priority. [code]FLAG_READ_ONLY[/code] and [code]FLAG_CHEAT[/code] reject config files, the command line, and the console. [method set_value] still works. Cheat variables accept those sources only in debug builds. Command text understands [code]name[/code], [code]name value[/code], [code]name=value[/code], [code]help [filter][/code], [code]dump [filter][/code], and [code]reset name[/code]. Separate several commands with [code];[/code]. A semicolon inside quotes stays part of the value. Names are case-insensitive. Startup arguments, parsed before user arguments: [codeblock] godot --cvar t.TimeScale=0.2 --cvar-exec "t.MaxFPS 30" --cvar-file user://cvars.cfg [/codeblock] [code]--cvar-file[/code] is read again while the game runs. [code]con.ConfigPollMs[/code] is the interval in milliseconds. On a windowed, non-editor run, [code]con.AutoConsole[/code] adds an in-game console toggled with [kbd]F1[/kbd] or the [kbd]`[/kbd] / [kbd]~[/kbd] key (the key to the left of 1). The default is on in debug builds and off in release builds. In the editor, [kbd]F1[/kbd] stays Search Help. Press that same [kbd]`[/kbd] / [kbd]~[/kbd] key when a text field is not focused, or use Editor > Toggle CVar Console. If a game is running and the debugger is connected, the same command is sent to that game. Built-in variables [code]t.TimeScale[/code] and [code]t.MaxFPS[/code] write through to [Engine] immediately. A remote debugger can run a command by sending a [code]cvar[/code] capture message [code]exec[/code] with the command string as its first argument. Variables named before they are registered (from the command line or a config file) are applied when [method register_variable] runs.

method.name: execute
method.description: Runs [param command] at console priority and returns the output text. Unknown names are an error. Use this from the in-game console and from scripts.

method.name: get_config_file
method.description: Returns the config file path set with [method set_config_file] or [code]--cvar-file[/code].

method.name: get_set_by
method.description: Returns the priority of the last accepted write to [param name]. Missing names return [constant SET_BY_CONSTRUCTOR].

method.name: get_value
method.description: Returns the current value of [param name], or [code]null[/code] if it is not registered.

method.name: has_command
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param name] is a registered command.

method.name: has_variable
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param name] is a registered variable.

method.name: help
method.description: Returns every variable and command whose name contains [param filter], plus a one-line syntax reminder. The match is case-insensitive. An empty filter lists everything.

method.name: register_command
method.description: Registers a command. [param callback] receives one [PackedStringArray] of arguments and may return a [String] to print. Returns [code]false[/code] if the name is invalid, empty, or already used.

method.name: register_variable
method.description: Registers a variable. [param default_value] must be an int, float, bool, or [String]; that type is fixed for later writes. A value previously supplied on the command line or in a config file is applied immediately. Returns [code]false[/code] if the name is invalid or already used.

method.name: reload_config_file
method.description: Reads the config file now and applies changed lines at config-file priority. Returns the output text, or an empty string if the file is missing or unchanged.

method.name: reset
method.description: Restores [param name] to its default and drops its priority back to constructor, so config files and the command line can write it again. Fails for unknown names, and for read-only or cheat variables when the console is not allowed to write them.

method.name: set_changed_callback
method.description: Calls [param callback] with [code](name, value)[/code] after a write changes the stored value. Returns [code]false[/code] if [param name] is not a variable.

method.name: set_config_file
method.description: Sets the file used by [method reload_config_file] and by the runtime poll. Changing the path forces the next read to apply the file again.

method.name: set_value
method.description: Writes [param value] at code priority. This can replace a command-line value and other values with the same or lower priority. Returns [code]false[/code] if the name is missing, the value cannot be converted, or a higher priority has already written the value.

method.name: set_value_with_priority
method.description: Writes [param value] at an explicit priority. Returns [code]false[/code] if a higher priority value is already stored, the variable is missing, or the source is blocked by [code]FLAG_READ_ONLY[/code] or [code]FLAG_CHEAT[/code].

method.name: unregister
method.description: Removes a variable or command. Pending startup values for that name are dropped too.

constants.constant: Config files, the command line, and the console cannot change this variable unless the build allows cheat commands. Debug builds allow them. Release builds do not. [method set_value] still can.
Config files, the command line, and the console cannot change this variable. [method set_value] still can.

The value can be read from the render thread. Integer variables with this flag must fit in a signed 32-bit integer. C++ code that needs a lock-free load should register an atomic reference instead of polling the singleton.
Default stored at registration. Lowest priority.
Value taken from project configuration, such as the project's max FPS.
Value written by [method execute] or the in-game console. Highest priority.
